summary: A feature published September 5, 2023 explores treasured family dessert recipes and the baking secrets, stories and traditions passed down with them. It profiles families and bakers across the US, including a Charleston blackberry cobbler, a San Francisco tres leches Bake-Off, a Leavenworth apfelstrudel bakery and a Vietnamese-French fusion crème brûlée. It also covers the science and art of baking, the difficulty of deciphering vague old recipes, and the frustrations and joys of baking heirloom desserts.
one_line: A 2023 feature on family dessert recipes and baking secrets, profiling families and bakers who preserve, decipher and modernize heirloom sweets.
key_facts: The article was published on September 5, 2023 under the topic Regional Cuisine and Recipes.
Martha Stewart (84, no relation to the celebrity homemaker) of Charleston, South Carolina has guarded her family's dessert recipe book since 1971.
Martha Stewart's blackberry cobbler is a family heirloom for more than a century; her secret is handpicked blackberries from the family farm, a tip from her grandmother.
The Rodriguez family of San Francisco holds an annual November "Bake-Off" that began in 1985, when Juan Rodriguez Sr. wanted his children to learn the family's tres leches cake.
Juan Rodriguez III said on November 15, 2023 that the Bake-Off is now more about bonding than baking, and the family updates the recipe yearly while keeping its essence.
New York City pastry chef Emily Thompson said on September 18, 2023 that baking is both a science and an art, and highlighted the "hand-me-down" technique that is hard to articulate or document.
The Schmitt family bakery in Leavenworth, Washington dates back to October 6, 1947; Johannes Schmitt immigrated from Germany and brought the apfelstrudel recipe.
Anna Schmitt, great-granddaughter of Johannes Schmitt, runs the bakery and says the key to the strudel is stretching the dough very thin; she also layers apples and uses breadcrumbs to soak up juice.

Ruth Goldberg, met on October 25, 2023, inherited her great-grandmother's lemon pound cake recipe with vague instructions like "bake until done" and "add flour to make a stiff batter", which she deciphered through trial and error.

In Austin, Texas, the Nguyen family, who migrated in the late 1980s, blends Vietnamese flavors into French-inspired pastries; on September 12, 2023 Chloe Nguyen showed a crème brûlée with pandan and coconut.
Variations in ovens, altitudes and egg sizes can throw old recipes off, causing frustrations like flopped cakes or cookies that spread too thin.
The article concludes that recipes are guidelines and baking them connects people to their lineage and family bonds.
